title: Execution Sentinel and Streaming Adapter for Multi-Tool Chains
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Problem: As customers compose multiple tool/function calls in a single streaming session, we see two classes of failure modes: (1) uncontrolled recursive/tool-reentry loops that escalate token usage and cause latency spikes; (2) inconsistent result injection semantics between hosted and private deployments that break structured-output contracts. Goal: Implement an Execution Sentinel (lightweight runtime monitor) plus a Streaming Adapter compatibility shim that enforces idempotency leashes, deterministic result-injection ordering, and a recursion detection policy. This ticket covers design, runtime implementation, API compatibility layer, metrics, and staged rollout. Scope: - Runtime: sentinel process that tracks tool invocation graph per request, enforces max-invocations, detects repeated tool argument fingerprints, and applies configurable backoff/fallbacks. - Streaming Adapter: compatibility layer that normalizes function-calling streaming frames and enforces the structured-output envelope across hosted/dedicated/private. - API: add optional request flags (max_tool_calls, injection_mode) with backward-compatible defaults. - Observability: new telemetry (tool_call_count, injection_latency_p50/p95, recursion_triggers) and tracing tags. Out of scope: redesign of tool SDKs; deep model-level hallucination detection (separate feature).
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel blocks repeated tool call chains that exceed configurable threshold and returns a well-defined structured error with code TOOL_RECURSION_DETECTED
Streaming Adapter emits normalized function_call frames across deployments so existing clients see identical structured outputs
New metrics (tool_call_count, recursion_triggers, injection_latency_p95) are available in Console per-route and per-request id
Backward compatibility: default behavior identical to current platform unless request opts into strict_injection=true
E2E tests cover common multi-tool flows including streaming partial results, out-of-order tool completions, and cancellation mid-stream
implementation_notes: Sentinel state kept in per-request ephemeral KV with bounded size; eviction policy LRU for tool call metadata
Recursion detection uses (tool_name + canonicalized_args_hash) with sliding-window counts; default max repeats = 3
Injection modes: permissive (current behavior), strict (disallow injected raw text outside structured envelope), fallback (convert to summarized placeholder and call fallback model)
Streaming Adapter will translate older function_call frames into new structured_output frames and carry an X-compat-version header
We will avoid cross-request global locks; all enforcement is request-scoped to preserve throughput
tradeoffs: Performance vs safety: sentinel adds ~1-2ms bookkeeping per tool call in microbenchmarks; acceptable for P1 routes but we will gate by config for latency-sensitive customers
Strict injection mode increases compatibility but may surface more errors to integrators; default remains permissive to avoid breaking existing users
State management: keeping sentinel state in-memory vs. external store. We choose in-memory per-worker to avoid network overhead; this increases worker memory but keeps latency low
risk: Misclassification of legitimate repeated calls (e.g., polling workflows) as recursion; mitigation: allow explicit whitelist via request header
Inconsistent behavior across Dedicated/private if not all nodes are upgraded; mitigation: Streaming Adapter signals compatibility level in response headers and falls back to permissive semantics
Potential for increased memory usage under high fanout; mitigation: strict per-request size caps and circuit-breakers
rollout_plan: Canary 1: enable sentinel in permissive mode on non-critical routes for 24h (telemetry validation)
Canary 2: enable strict_injection flag for internal customers + SDK alpha for 1 week
Gradual: enable default permissive sentinel globally, expose strict_injection via API and console toggles
Enterprise: provide migration guide for Dedicated/private upgrades with compatibility header checks
testing_plan: Unit tests for sentinel state transitions and recursion heuristics
Integration tests for streaming adapter that replay recorded multi-tool sessions from production traces
Load test: high-concurrency streaming sessions with mixed tool fanout to validate memory caps and latency impact
Client compatibility tests across SDK versions (node, python) verifying structured_output envelope
